transcript.text: dyson keeps pulsin on n off like its stutterin, wont stay on proper. batt is full. pls help

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. That pulsing sound is the vacuum's protection system kicking in because it thinks there is a blockage or a filter issue. Since your battery is fully charged, we need to check if airflow is restricted. First, please empty the bin and remove the filters (pre-motor and HEPA). Wash them in cold water only—no soap—and leave them somewhere warm and dry for at least 24 hours. Even a little dampness will cause this stuttering. While they are drying, could you tell me the model number of your Dyson? It is usually on a label on the body of the machine.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — A vacuum that pulses or cuts out after running is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage starving the airflow — check and clear those before suspecting battery, charger or motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its a v8 animal. no burning smell or heat from it btw. ok ill try the filter, its grey tho not purple

The grey colour on your V8 Animal filters is normal; they are not purple like some other models. Since there is no heat or burning smell, the motor isn't overheating yet. The pulsing is probably because the vacuum detects restricted airflow and cuts power to protect itself. While you leave the filters drying for 24 hours (they must be completely bone-dry), please detach the wand and floorhead and look through the tube and bin inlet to check for a blockage like a coin or debris. Did you find anything stuck?
yeah found a big clump of hair and cat litter stuck at the bottom of the wand where the head goes on, pulled it out. suction seems ok now?

Yes, that sounds exactly right. Just a quick tip: cat litter can be very abrasive and clog filters quickly, so try to keep the bin as empty as possible and check the wand occasionally. If it starts stuttering again even when everything is clear, let me know—but for now, you should be good to go!

candidates: Blocked airway or damp filter triggering protection mode (high)
